first_fatal_error.detail: The strongest result actually proved is Corollary 6: max gcd(m_i,m_j) >= k^{1/3} unconditionally, and >= c*sqrt(k)/log k conditional on Mertens/Rosser–Schoenfeld. The cell-6 target requires one of: (a) deciding a size k >= 25; (b) gcd >= ck for an absolute c > 0, or an improvement of the known factor k*exp(-(2+o(1)) log k/log log k) (i.e. something better than k^{1-o(1)}); (c) the group form at k = 6. A bound of order k^{1/2-o(1)} is strictly weaker than the already-known k^{1-o(1)} and does not touch (a) or (c). The submission's own remarks concede that the recursion of Lemma 4 cannot give better than F(g) ≲ g^2/2, i.e. gcd ≳ sqrt(2k), so no route to the target is present. The declared claim 'main' is therefore not established, and no other reusable claim was declared.

report.math_notes: Checked line by line; the internal mathematics is correct. Lemma 1 (gcd >= 2) is immediate from (*). Lemma 2: if no prime lies in [P,g] any two members would need a common prime factor q <= g < P dividing m_i, contradicting coprimality — correct. Lemma 3: the affine injection y -> r+py carries b_i + n_i Z onto a_i + m_i Z (r + p b_i = a_i), so disjointness is inherited, gcd scales by exactly p, and divisors of n_i divide m_i — correct. Lemma 4: the partition K_1..K_{s+1} by smallest prime factor in [P,g] is well defined; K_{s+1} = ∅ because any i with a partner j shares a prime q in [P,g] (q >= P by admissibility, q <= gcd <= g); each K_t ∩ J_{p_t,r} maps to an admissible family for S(floor(g/p_t), p_t) (gcd <= g/p_t and integer, coprimality to primes < p_t from the definition of K_t plus admissibility); the union bound over t and r gives R(g,P). Finiteness by induction on g is fine since floor(g/p_t) < g. Theorem 5(A): sum over primes of 1/p^2 < sum_{n>=2} 1/(n(n-1)) = 1 — correct. Theorem 5(B): Q(floor(g/p_t),p_t) <= Q_t since factors >= 1; (1+2/p)/p <= 2/p for p >= 2 gives Q_t/p_t <= Q_t - Q_{t+1}; telescoping to Q_1 - 1 < Q_1 — correct. Corollary 6(1) g >= k^{1/3} follows. Corollary 6(2) is correct conditional on the cited Rosser–Schoenfeld bound (stated with hypotheses x > 1, B = 0.2614...); the constant 13.53 checks (2B + 1/log^2 2 ≈ 2.604, e^{2.604} ≈ 13.52), and the case split g >= sqrt(k) vs g < sqrt(k) is valid for k >= 2 since 4 log k > 1. Side remark verified: R(2,2) = 2·S(1,2) = 2, so Lemma 4 alone does prove the k = 3 statement (cell 1), but that is not a declared claim in this submission. The trusted rerun of code_1 only evaluates the recursion R(g,2) for g <= 3000 and is a consistency check, not part of any proof; it proves nothing universal. If the researcher wants credit for the established partial results, they should declare separate claims, e.g. 'Lemma 4 recursion S(g,P) <= R(g,P)', 'F(g) <= g^3 for all g', and 'max gcd >= c sqrt(k)/log k (conditional on Rosser–Schoenfeld)'; as written these would be acceptable, but none of them meets the cell-6 target.
